No retirement in any clean or noisy condition (0 in 6 conditions x 20 worlds for every arm with retirement): in those worlds a rule the guard accepted is never contradicted by most of its recent answers. Over all report runs, 351 retirements, all of rules that were stale at that moment, 0 of rules still right. The current learner (no B7) has no stale rules at the end even under strong drift (its sequence rules survived the regime changes here), so retirement alone changes nothing for it (learner+retire minus learner: +0.000, 20 ties, in all three strong-drift conditions). Wrong at acceptance: 0 sequence rules in every arm; 1 constant in "all" medium drift60 and 1 in B7-all large hard60 (both arms, of 66 to 144 constants), a B7 property under strong drift, not caused by retirement.

Strong drift, reward per energy: B7-all 2.801 / 2.814 / 2.950 (medium drift60 / large drift60 / large hard60), B7+retire 2.824 / 2.821 / 2.960, all 2.860 / 2.819 / 2.927, oracle-knows-rules 3.249 / 3.333 / 3.515. B7+retire minus B7-all: **+0.023 [+0.005, +0.041] 7/0/13** (medium drift60), +0.007 [-0.014, +0.028] 9/3/8, +0.011 [-0.004, +0.025] 7/4/9; all minus B7-all: +0.059 [-0.173, +0.291], +0.005 [-0.178, +0.188], -0.023 [-0.180, +0.135].

B3b changes (switches and prior conflicts) per 20 worlds: 37 (small clean) to 136 (large drift) with B7 (a prior conflict is not a world change, see Track B3b).

### Verdict

* **All skills together are not better than B7 alone.** All minus the current learner: +0.175 to +0.436, interval above 0 in 6 of 12 conditions (all four medium ones, small noisy and small drift; small clean -0.003 at the lower end), about the B7 gain. All minus B7-all: -0.104 to +0.076, interval containing 0 in 11 of 12, and below 0 in medium noisy (-0.057 [-0.090, -0.024], worse in 18 of 20). The gap to oracle-knows-rules stays +0.20 to +0.50 (oracle better in 18 to 20 of 20 worlds everywhere).
* **B9 does not pay off with B7 on.** Its faster discovery still adds sequence rules (0 wrong) but no reward: B7+B9 minus B7-all -0.111 to +0.083, significantly negative in medium noisy (-0.047 [-0.080, -0.015]); the interaction with B7 is -0.084 to +0.062, no interval excludes 0. Most sequence rules duplicate `careful` (Track B7), and experiments take energy from the formula families where the fitted constants pay. At the B9 setting kappa 0.25 the loss was larger on the tuning seeds.
* **B3b on top of B7: no gain, small measurable costs.** -0.022 to +0.007; below 0 by 0.004 to 0.007 in medium clean, large clean and large noisy (intervals just below 0). The B3b gain in its own world (+0.027) came from hard cells after visible changes; in World v2 the B7 parts already decide most of the rule cells.
* **B8 on top of everything: mostly worse.** All + B8 minus all: -0.080 to +0.071; below 0 in small noisy (-0.080 [-0.126, -0.034]), small hard (-0.076 [-0.143, -0.010]) and medium hard (-0.080 [-0.149, -0.011]), worse in 14 to 18 of 20 worlds in every condition. Same as in Track B8: no lookahead benefit in a world that was not built around unlocks.
* **Retirement works as a safety mechanism, with little reward effect.** It retired only stale rules (351 of 351, 0 false retirements, none in clean or noisy worlds) and roughly halved the stale rules left at the end under drift (8 -> 5, 10 -> 6, 25 -> 14, 25 -> 15; strong drift 30 -> 14, 53 -> 25, 57 -> 32), raising the share right of rule answers by 0.2 to 2.8 points; reward +0.000 to +0.009 in the standard conditions (no interval excludes 0) and +0.023 [+0.005, +0.041] in medium drift60 (the only significant gain), +0.007 and +0.011 elsewhere under strong drift. The A estimate already lowers the use of a stale rule through its reported failures, which is why removing it adds little reward.
* **Conflicts found:** B9 competes with C/G for energy (above); B8's hybrid future term favours cheap options in the noisy and hard conditions (as in B8's `probe` setting); B3b's prior cut and B7's rule resets touch the same `discovered` cells (a rule acceptance or retirement now also clears that cell's B3b window, by design). Nothing broke a cap or the replay (tests below).

Read with the limits: one author wrote the world, all the parts, their tuning and this measurement; two settings were tuned on seeds 101..120 (about 11 settings); 20 worlds per condition; the strong-drift conditions were added for retirement after seeing that the standard ones have few stale rules. The recommended controller for World v2 from these numbers is `rules_use = on` (with or without `rule_retirement = on`) and the other parts off; the profile is still useful as a test that everything runs together within the caps.

### What is tested (not measured)

`world2/tests_all.rs`, `world2/skills.rs`, `being_v2_all_tools_tests.rs`: with every part off the all-skills run writes exactly what `run_v2` writes (log digest), and a default being's genesis carries no B10 tag; the three published reports (`measure_world_v2`, `measure_rules_use`, `measure_experiment`) are byte-identical before and after the change (checked once by hand on this branch); the B3b model in World v2 equals `model.rs` in mode `Switch` bit for bit over 4000 observations with both mechanisms firing; the grant fails closed (no file, invalid file, valid file without the keys: everything off, 5 refusals), each part needs its own key, an existing being keeps its creation-time switches (refused otherwise); with everything on (lookahead off), two logged runs are identical, the state folded from the log equals the live state, every learner and experimenter decision replays, every rule and constant is re-derived from the examples logged before it (with the retired signatures' old examples left out), every retirement has a revision citing the rule's note and at least one failing outcome, every model change a revision, the profile note says what was on and what was refused; the kill switch stops the all-skills run (lookahead on) before the next step (30 steps when it turns on at the 31st check) and is logged; the caps hold together: live rules, energy per run, the experiment budget and the lookahead node cap, each with its refusal in the log; retirement retires (mostly stale) rules under drift, none in clean worlds, never when off; the observer's counts (steps, energy, experiments, rules accepted / retired, rule answers, model changes, stops, refusals) equal the run's and it writes nothing; tool level: the profile without the keys runs with every part off and audits five refusals, with the keys everything is on, a bad profile name writes nothing, KILL refuses the run and is audited while `being_observe` still answers; `being_observe` is allowed by `authorize()` for the thinker only when the owner lists it (also under KILL, as a read-only tool), denied otherwise and audited.

### What B10 does not show

A benefit of combining the parts (none was found); any world other than World v2; whether a different combination of settings (tuned jointly rather than one part at a time) would help; replay of lookahead decisions; real data or a real thinker.

## Track B11: open-ended world and the long-run decline (synthetic worlds, author-defined rewards)

Branch `open-world` (from 4feb8daf), 2026-11-07, Windows, 8 CPUs, machine shared with other work. Measured with
`cargo run -p kore-self --example measure_b11 --offline --release -- decline|b1|worldo|worldo-log` (modes described
in the file head). All runs in-process; run data under `kw\openworld-data` (not committed). Design of World O:
`docs/open_world.md`.

### Part 1: why reward per energy declines in a stationary world (bug 4 of docs/longrun.md)

Reproduction: `being/measure_b11.rs` steps the long run's being in-process (world 1, extended2 families, chooser
model, discovery every 10 steps, composition and pruning under the long-run controller, budget 3000 with refills)
through the normal `Engine::step_menu`, with a side channel that is never logged: per step, the decision of a renewal
oracle on the same offers (knows the hidden success rates and real energy; takes the option of highest
`reward x p - rho x energy`, skips when that is below `-rho x 1`; `rho` found by iterating `rho <- its own rate`:
4.220 in world 1, above the grid skip oracle of docs/longrun.md, 4.158), the loss of each step in those terms (split
into skip decisions and option choice), the optimism bonus and the skip bar. The first 300,000 steps give the long
run's numbers (0-100k 4.096 here; the long run's two 50k windows 4.095 and 4.098).

World 1, 1,000,000 steps, windows of 100,000 steps (B1 skip test):

| steps | reward per energy | regret vs renewal oracle | attempt share (oracle 0.577-0.580) | over-skips per 1000 steps | loss from skip decisions / option choice per 1000 steps | bonus of the attempted option | skip bar | mean abs error of p on attempts |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-100k | 4.096 | +0.123 | 0.427 | 150.9 | 288.8 / 0.3 | 0.0170 | 4.086 | 0.0020 |
| 100-200k | 4.091 | +0.128 | 0.420 | 161.0 | 320.7 / 0.0 | 0.0062 | 4.096 | 0.0014 |
| 300-400k | 4.052 | +0.168 | 0.402 | 176.1 | 378.4 / 0.0 | 0.0035 | 4.082 | 0.0011 |
| 500-600k | 4.025 | +0.195 | 0.391 | 187.2 | 417.2 / 0.0 | 0.0026 | 4.076 | 0.0011 |
| 700-800k | 4.044 | +0.175 | 0.398 | 179.5 | 390.6 / 0.0 | 0.0024 | 4.073 | 0.0010 |
| 900k-1M | 4.020 | +0.200 | 0.387 | 191.2 | 434.1 / 0.0 | 0.0019 | 4.066 | 0.0009 |

Cause (confirmed by these numbers): the whole regret is in skip decisions; option choice costs nothing after 100k
steps. The B1 planner skips when the best optimistic score is below the full realized rate (about 4.07 to 4.09, close
to constant because it is the cumulative rate). But a skip costs energy too: both "attempt" and "skip" lead to a fresh
menu, so the attempt is worth it when `reward x p > rate x (energy - 1)`, i.e. the right bar is about
`rate x (1 - 1/energy)` (3.0 here). Early, the optimism `beta x sd` of the options it attempts lifts many good offers
over the too-strict bar; that bonus shrinks with the evidence (0.0170 -> 0.0019, about 1/sqrt(n)), so offers that pay
more than a skip saves fall below the bar one cell at a time, and a skipped cell gets no new data. The attempt share
falls (0.427 -> 0.387) while the oracle's stays at 0.577, and over-skips rise (151 -> 191 per 1000 steps). The
hypothesis of docs/longrun.md (shrinking bonus, fixed bar) is right, with the addition that the bar was too strict
from the start. Ruled out: estimate drift (the error of the attempted cells' p falls 0.0020 -> 0.0009), counts or float
precision (u64 counts; f64 sums of integers stay far below 2^53), forgetting (none in this mode). The decline is not
monotone (a cumulative bar moves slowly and lets cells back in now and then: 4.087 at 400-500k, 4.085 at 600-700k).

Fix (opt-in, `planner::SkipRule`, default `Rate` = B1): `Calibrated` uses the bar `rate x (1 - SKIP_COST / e)` with
`e` the estimated energy of the best option; `Settled(k)` moves from the B1 bar to the calibrated one as the best
option's own cell fills up: `rate x (1 - w x SKIP_COST / e)`, `w = n / (n + k)`. Choice of k on tuning seeds 101..120
only (B1 menu world, budgets 600 / 3000, difference to the B1 test): calibrated -0.118 / +0.079; k = 10 -0.008 /
+0.085; 30 +0.001 / +0.071; **100 +0.004 / +0.058**; 300 +0.006 / +0.044; 1000 -0.001 / +0.028. k = 100 was taken
(no loss at the short budget, worse in 4 of 20 there).

Short runs, report seeds 1..20 (B1 menu world, mean [95% interval]; the B1 skip test gives exactly the documented
3.117 and 3.377):

| budget | B1 skip test | calibrated | calibrated minus B1 (better / equal / worse) | settled k=100 | settled minus B1 (better / equal / worse) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 600 | 3.117 [2.757, 3.477] | 3.016 [2.684, 3.348] | -0.101 [-0.163, -0.039] (1 / 0 / 19) | 3.118 [2.759, 3.477] | +0.001 [-0.007, +0.009] (5 / 9 / 6) |
| 3000 | 3.377 [3.057, 3.697] | 3.420 [3.074, 3.766] | +0.043 [+0.001, +0.086] (12 / 0 / 8) | 3.425 [3.087, 3.764] | +0.049 [+0.010, +0.087] (14 / 0 / 6) |

Long runs, 1,000,000 steps in-process, worlds 1..8 (the long-run settings; n = 8, intervals over worlds), reward per
energy in the second window (100-200k) and the last (900k-1M):

| skip test | second window | last window | last minus second | whole run after the first window, minus B1 (paired) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| B1 (`rate`) | 4.023 [3.702, 4.344] | 3.973 [3.629, 4.317] | -0.050 [-0.130, +0.030] | - |
| calibrated | 4.576 [4.022, 5.129] | 4.500 [3.960, 5.039] | -0.076 [-0.200, +0.047] | +0.556 [+0.286, +0.826] |
| settled k=100 | 4.212 [3.871, 4.553] | 4.172 [3.796, 4.548] | -0.040 [-0.126, +0.047] | +0.208 [+0.066, +0.350] |

World 1 with `settled`: 4.164, 4.167, 4.166, 4.161, 4.170, 4.148, 4.168, 4.160, 4.159, 4.152 per 100k window (B1:
4.096 -> 4.020), regret +0.055 to +0.072, attempt share 0.466-0.467 in every window, over-skips 111-113 per 1000
steps in every window. With `calibrated` world 1 is at 4.182-4.205 (regret +0.014 to +0.038). Per world, second
window -> last window with `settled`: 4.167 -> 4.152, 4.609 -> 4.614, 3.563 -> 3.569, 3.842 -> 3.515, 4.398 -> 4.420,
3.726 -> 3.732, 4.824 -> 4.803, 4.567 -> 4.573. The fall in world 4 (both skip tests, at 400k steps: B1 3.780 ->
3.309) comes with a rule retired by the long-run pruning (live rules 11 -> 10) and a jump of the option-choice loss
(42 -> 281 per 1000 steps) and of the estimate error (0.005 -> 0.036): a different effect, not studied here. With the
B1 test the decline across the 8 worlds is small and its interval contains 0; world 1, the long run's world, has the
clearest one.

Verdict: cause found (a skip bar that is too strict, hidden early by the optimism bonus); `settled` removes the
decline in world 1 and earns more in long runs (+0.208 over worlds 1..8) without a loss at budget 600 and with a
small gain at 3000. `calibrated` gains more in long runs but loses at budget 600 (19 of 20 worlds). Off by default; the
first world's genesis does not record the switch, so it is not available through the binary (`being_run`).

Steps: the learner spends about 2 energy per step (attempt share 0.37-0.41, it skips most menus), so 1,000,000 steps
are about 2,000,000 energy units; the window 250-500k energy is about steps 80,000-180,000. Whole run after the first
window: fix minus current -0.109 [-0.344, +0.126] (1 of 5 better), fix+b7 minus current -0.178 [-0.340, -0.015]. Top
tier Spearman (index vs attempts to competence): +0.019 [-0.095, +0.133] (current). Rules accepted per world: 207
(current), 125 (fix), 67 (fix+b7); 93.8% of rule answers right.

Logged run (`worldo-log`, seed 1, learner `current`, real versioned log in format 3, chunks of 5,000 steps, every
chunk a cold restart that re-folds the state from the log, KILL file before the call that would cross 30,000 steps):
12 calls of 5,000 steps (60,000 steps) plus one call refused by the KILL file
(0 steps, `stop:kill_switch` note logged); 13 to 56 s per call on the shared machine, growing with the log (every call
reads and folds the whole log); 49.3 MB and 12,000 files at 60,000 steps (about 820 bytes per step). At the end:
`verify` ok, outcome steps consecutive from 0 to 59,999, all 60,000 decisions re-derived from the log alone with 0
mismatches, 68 rule notes, 74 family notes, 0 refusals. The 1,000,000-step target was not run on a log (the full read
at every call makes each call slower as the log grows; World O has no streamed restart path).

Verdict: **the learning curve does not keep rising; it flattens and falls behind.** In World O the learner keeps up
with the reference while the families are simple (regret 0.10-0.13 in the first 100k-250k energy) and then falls
behind once almost all families are of the top tier: regret 0.4 to 1.0 from about 300,000 energy units (roughly
100,000 to 150,000 steps) on, reward per energy flat at about 4.0 to 4.6 while the reference sits at 4.7 to 5.1.
There is no sign that it learns new families faster after having seen more of them (correlation about 0, the first-10
ratio does not rise, the share of families it ever becomes competent on falls). Neither the skip fix nor the B7
switches help here (both are worse on the mean; B7 significantly). The gap to the reference is mostly rule knowledge
(oracle-planner without rules is close to the learners); the being accepts fewer rules per window as the life goes
on. B3b adaptation is not available for the family-keyed model and was not run. Not tested: why the rule acceptances
fall (candidate: fewer attempts, hence fewer examples, on new families that start from the pooled prior and are
skipped), a cold-start bonus for new families in the family-keyed model.

### What is tested (not measured)

`being/tests_b11.rs`: the skip switch is off by default and the B1 report means at budgets 600 and 3000 are unchanged
(3.117, 3.377); the bars (settled at n = 0 is the B1 bar, at large n the calibrated one); `settled` attempts more,
over-skips less and earns more than B1 in world 1 (12,000 steps). `being/world_o/tests.rs`: World O is a pure function
of its config; the schedule (open slots distinct, compose bases open and outliving their children, tiers
non-decreasing, all tiers, compose and drift present, config validation and tag round trip); the checkers against an
independent statement of each rule; `LearnerO` with the default test is `Learner2` step for step over 1,500 steps;
the fold of a logged run equals the live state, every decision is re-derived from the log (2,500 of 2,500), a run of
2,500 steps equals 1,200 + 1,300 with a cold restart (same rows), for both skip tests; caps (live rules), KILL before
the first step and after 12 steps, energy cap, end of budget; World v2 and World O rows in one log fold independently;
the references are deterministic and oracle-knows-rules beats oracle-planner and the learner.

### What B11 does not show

Anything outside these author-defined worlds; the skip fix through the real binary; World O through the real binary
(there is no MCP tool for it); World O with feedback noise; a learner that keeps up in World O.

## Track B12: learning to learn (synthetic world, author-defined families)

Everything here is the World O simulation (`docs/open_world.md`: author-defined families, grammar, schedule, drift
and rewards) and the being's own learner. Question: in World O new task families keep appearing, and Track B11
found that the being does not get faster at learning later families (top-tier Spearman of family order vs
attempts to competence +0.025 [-0.060, +0.110]), its competent share falls from 84% to 47-49% on the last top-tier
families and its regret against `oracle-knows-rules` rises from 0.13 to 0.84 per window. Can it reuse experience
across families so that later families are learned faster? Code: `kore-self/src/being/world_o/b12.rs` (new), hooks in
`world_o/engine.rs` (switch-guarded), one default no-op trait method in `world2/learner.rs` (`Chooser2::prepare_o`),
measurement `world_o/measure_b12.rs` and `examples/measure_b12.rs` (modes `diag`, `report`, `seqdebug`), observer
`being_observe --source being:worldo` / `--demo-o`. Branch `learn-to-learn` (from a4ca4231), 2026-11-07, Windows, 8
CPUs shared with other work. Tuning seeds 101..120 (diagnosis on all 20, tuning on 101..110 at a 600,000-energy
life), report seeds 1..20 at the B11 life of 1,200,000 energy units, windows of 100,000, 95% t-intervals of the mean,
paired differences on identical worlds. Score: TRUE reward per energy (the checker's verdict). Controller of every run:
live-rule cap 200, candidate cap 100,000, no composition (as B11).

A fix needed first: the merge of B10 and B11 into brain-v5 did not compile (`LearnerOCfg::w2()` lacked the B10
`skills` field); the one-line fix (`skills: Default::default()`) is part of this branch.

### Step 1: diagnosis (cause confirmed, but not the candidate one)

`measure_b12 diag` (seeds 101..120, `current` learner) records, for every family, the first 100 menus on which it
appears: how often the being attempts it, skips the menu, the examples it gives, the being's starting estimate of the
truly best strategy against that strategy's true success rate, and whether the starting score is below the skip bar.
`seqdebug` lists, for the open sequence families at a few points of one life, the examples per (family, difficulty)
and which grammar form explains them.

| families (seeds 101..120, pooled) | n | attempts on it per menu | menus skipped per menu | start estimate p | true p | start score below the skip bar | sequence families never given a rule |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| tiers 0-1 | 320 | 0.260 | 0.265 | 0.703 | 0.778 | 39% | 68% |
| tiers 2-3 | 320 | 0.282 | 0.276 | 0.707 | 0.532 | 6% | 71% |
| tier 4, index 32-95 | 1280 | 0.230 | 0.343 | 0.712 | 0.510 | 6% | 71% |
| tier 4, index 96-159 | 1280 | 0.186 | 0.491 | 0.710 | 0.522 | 9% | 84% |
| tier 4, index 160+ | 860 | 0.179 | 0.502 | 0.698 | 0.528 | 8% | 84% |

Per type at the top tier the pooled starting estimate is too optimistic for sequence (+0.21 to +0.26), compose
(+0.18 to +0.23) and formula families (+0.60 to +0.64), too pessimistic for grids (-0.25 to -0.34), about right for
knapsacks.

* The candidate cause of B11 ("new families start from a pooled prior and are skipped") is **not** what happens:
  the starting estimate is too *optimistic* for the families that need rules (only 5-9% of top-tier families start
  below the skip bar), and a new top-tier sequence family is attempted on 11 to 14 of its first 100 menus
  (10.9 to 14.4 examples). What falls over the life is the attempt share once those first tries fail (0.230 ->
  0.179 per menu; menus skipped 0.34 -> 0.50).
* The cause of the missing rules: the B2 search keys a rule by (family, difficulty) and needs 3 training + 1
  held-out examples **in one such signature**; a family's examples spread over five difficulties. `seqdebug`
  (seed 101) shows it directly: e.g. at 300,000 energy a tribonacci family has 2, 2, 2, 2, 2 examples at
  difficulties 1-5 and a cubic one 2, 2, 3, 3, 4; in every such case the right form explains every example at every
  difficulty, but no signature reaches 3 + 1 (at a window end 1.4 to 7.0, after 400,000 energy units 1.4 to 2.4, of the 15 to 21 signatures with examples
  hold at least 4 examples). 77% of all sequence families never get a rule (84% after family 96),
  and a `compose` family (reusing a base family's rule at the same difficulty) can only use the rule where the base
  has one at that difficulty.
* Rule-search inputs fall with the attempt share: examples held at window ends 741-1,319 in the first 400,000 energy,
  226-1,339 later; rules accepted per window 7.3, 14.4, 17.1, 9.2, then 2.9 to 6.2.

So the being does not reuse what one difficulty of a family teaches about the others, nor what earlier families
teach about new ones: its knowledge of rules restarts per (family, difficulty), its estimates restart per family
from a prior pooled over every family ever seen.

### What was built (each a switch, off by default, `docs/open_world.md`)

| part | switch (genesis tag `wo_l2l:k/n/w/pm/f`) | what it does |
|---|---|---|
| M2 hierarchical prior | `prior_k` (8) | at a family's announcement, an empirical-Bayes Beta prior per (strategy, difficulty) from the latest 8 families of the same announced type (closed or open, >= 5 attempts with the strategy, >= 3 families; weight from their spread, 2..30), in place of the prior pooled over every family |
| M3 new-family exploration | `explore_n` (10), weight 0.5, budget 50 per mille | an information bonus `0.5 x rate x (1 - n/10)` on the options of a family with fewer than 10 attempts, while the energy of the steps the bonus changed (policy `wo-explore`) stays under 5% of the energy spent; the controller can lower the budget (`max_explore_pm`, refusal logged before the first step) |
| M4 level 1, family-wide rules | `form` = 1 (`fam`) | after the B2 pass, one form sought over all examples of a family (every difficulty) under the B2 guard (never applicable-and-wrong, 3 training + 1 held-out, the 3 spare equations), accepted for every difficulty of the family without a rule |
| M4 level 2, rule-form prior | `form` = 2 (`form`) | as level 1, and the forms accepted in >= 2 earlier families (and the family's own forms) are tried first and need 2 + 1 instead of 3 + 1 |

The constants were set before the report and checked on tuning seeds 101..110 (life 600,000), differences to the
current learner: with the defaults `prior` -0.068, `explore` +0.080, `fam` +0.371, `form` +0.385, `all` +0.372;
cohort 4 / 16 gave `prior+form` +0.203 / +0.137; a weaker exploration (weight 0.25, 6 tries) gave `all` +0.085. The
defaults were kept. Nothing was tuned on the report seeds.

### Verdict

Cause confirmed, and it is not the B11 candidate: new top-tier families are not skipped from the start (their
pooled starting estimate is too optimistic, not too pessimistic); the being's rules restart per (family,
difficulty), so a family's examples, spread over five difficulties, rarely reach the B2 support in any one of them
(77% of sequence families never got a rule). **Family-wide rules (M4) fix most of it**: +0.36 to +0.37 reward per
energy over the whole life (20 of 20 worlds), regret in the last window 0.836 -> 0.373 (0.268 with all switches),
competent share on the last top-tier families 47-49% -> 89-92%, 0 wrong rules among 7,471 judged (2,836 accepted
with the reduced support of the rule-form prior, 0 wrong). **Faster later?** The order-vs-competence correlation
turns negative (form -0.098 [-0.171, -0.026], paired -0.123 [-0.176, -0.070] against current), but it is small:
the gain is mostly immediate (each family's own difficulties share a form) and only a little of it grows with
experience of earlier families (level 2 over level 1: +0.005 reward, -0.014 Spearman). Regret still rises over the
life (form 0.195 -> 0.349, interval of the change contains 0). The hierarchical prior (M2) makes the first attempts
at a family much better (first-10 ratio 0.32-0.42 -> 0.51-0.61) but costs reward (-0.316 alone, and it halves the
gain of M4 in `prior+form`): an accurate, confident prior for families that start out hard removes the optimism
that made the being try them, so they give fewer examples (2.2 against 5.3 in their first 100 menus) and fewer
rules. Exploration (M3) changes little (-0.021 alone; +0.006 on top of M4). With the B11 skip fix and B7 on, all
B12 switches together gain only +0.085 [-0.028, +0.199] over current (+0.330 over fix+b7 itself), so the B7
switches still hurt in World O. Recommended combination from these numbers: `form` or `explore+form`, not M2.

### Other worlds

The B12 code is used only by World O (B12 is not wired into World v2 or the first world). With the switches off the
outputs of `measure_b11 worldo --seeds 1..3 --budget 60000 --window 20000` and `measure_b11 b1 --seeds 1..5` from the
binary built before B12 and the one built after are byte-identical (md5 5c7753f2... and ae3bb95d...), and the World
v2 tests (golden digests of Track B7) pass unchanged; the only edit outside World O is a default no-op trait method.
So World v2 and the B1 worlds are exactly as before; whether family-wide rules would help in World v2 was not
measured.

### Caveats

Author-defined world and grammar; M4 works because in World O the hidden class of a family is the same at every
difficulty (a world where it changes with the difficulty would see such forms rejected by the never-wrong guard,
and gain nothing); the wrong-rule judge samples 60 tasks at acceptance and does not follow a rule through its
family's drift; tiers are not observable, so M2 uses "the latest families of a type"; the constants were chosen on
10 tuning seeds at half the life; no long run (> 1.2M energy) and no logged run at full length with B12 on.

### What is tested (not measured)

`being/world_o/tests_b12.rs`: off by default and then the B11 being (the B12 measurement run equals `run_wo` window
for window; no B12 tag in a default log; empty B12 state; a pinned digest of a default run); the `wo_l2l` tag round
trip and refusal of bad tags; the empirical-Bayes prior (too few families: none; consistent families give a
stronger weight; only earlier families of the same type count; an empty cell's estimate is the prior's); family-wide
rules (four examples at four difficulties: B2 accepts nothing, level 1 accepts the form for all five difficulties,
a second pass adds nothing, an example the form gets wrong blocks it); the rule-form prior (three examples: nothing
without a prior, five reduced-support rules with the form seen in two earlier families, level 1 ignores the prior);
exploration (attempts happen, the energy stays within the budget, the controller cap is logged before the first
decision and holds, fold and replay with `wo-explore` decisions); with all switches on: fold of the log equals the
live state (priors formed, families closed), all 2,500 decisions re-derived from the log, 1,200 + 1,300 steps with a
cold restart equal 2,500, the live-rule cap holds, KILL before the first step and after 12 steps (stop logged).

## Track V1: versus standard methods (synthetic worlds, author-defined)

Question: where does the being's learner stand against well-known methods from the literature, implemented cleanly (Rust, no libraries) and tuned fairly, and against a language model, on the same worlds, seeds and budgets? Full description, sources, every table and the caveats: `docs/vs_world.md`. Code: `kore-self/src/being/vs_world/` (new), harness `kore-self/examples/measure_vs_world.rs`; one module line in `being/mod.rs`; a one-line merge fix in `world_o/engine.rs` (the crate did not compile at a4ca4231). Measured 2026-11-07, branch `vs-world` from a4ca4231. Report seeds 1..20, tuning seeds 101..120 (two passes per method family and world), 95% t-intervals, paired differences on identical worlds (better/worse/tie of 20).

Methods: decaying eps-greedy, UCB1-tuned, KL-UCB, Thompson sampling (Beta), EXP3, LinUCB (disjoint), linear Thompson, tabular Q-learning and SARSA (discounted semi-Markov or average-reward), a 32-unit MLP Q-learner with replay and a target network; each sees only the visible features the being's planner sees and the told (noisy) rewards, and uses only the fixed strategies (no rule book). References that see hidden information: MCTS (UCT) on the true simulator, and the existing oracles. Rule learning: brute-force enumeration over the same DSL and guard, k-NN and regression trees on the same revealed examples. LLM: the Claude CLI (haiku alias) choosing each step, allowed to answer sequence tasks itself.

| LLM, World v2 small clean, budget 60, n = 3 (indicative) | current 0.457, recommended 0.456 | LLM 0.656 [-1.001, 2.312]; its own answers counted 1.200 | +0.20 [-2.24, +2.64] (LLM minus ours) | oracle-knows-rules 2.984 |

Verdict.
* **World v2: the current learner loses to a tuned linear contextual bandit; the recommended profile ties it.** LinUCB is above the current learner by 0.18 to 0.38 (11 of 12 conditions significant); B7 rule use plus the B11 skip fix close that gap (recommended minus LinUCB within -0.09 to +0.13, no interval excludes 0) and beat UCB1-tuned, KL-UCB (10 of 12 significant), eps-greedy (7), Thompson (6), and EXP3, Q-learning, SARSA, the MLP (12). The being's choosing part is the weaker part here; its rule use makes up for it. Oracle-knows-rules is still 0.19 to 0.57 above.
* **First world: loses at the short budget, ties at the long one.** At budget 600 LinUCB, eps-greedy and Thompson are above the being (-0.45, -0.30, -0.20, significant); at 3000 it ties LinUCB and beats the rest.
* **World L: the one-step planner is slightly below simple bandits everywhere; the lookahead wins only in the unlock setting** (keys 1600 +0.34), where no standard method, including the tabular Q-learners with the token in their state, learns the key -> vault chain.
* **World O: the being wins clearly.** The current learner is above every standard method by 0.54 to 3.10 after the first window (better in 18 to 20 of 20 worlds against each) and above the oracle-planner (+0.33), because World O keeps opening families whose rules the B2 search learns and the methods have no rules; the regret of every policy still grows as the families reach the top tier (methods 1.1 to 4.1 in the last window, current 0.81). No policy learns later families clearly faster.
* **Rule learning: the verified search is clearly ahead** of brute-force enumeration in the same DSL (+0.10 to +0.19 right share) and of k-NN and regression trees (+0.26 to +0.74), never answering wrong; under 10% noise the exact guard collapses with more examples (0.55 -> 0.03) and the B7 robust guard is needed (0.77 to 0.81).
* **LLM: nothing measurable.** n = 3 worlds of 11 steps; 31 calls in total (25 scored: 16 valid, 9 failed on the wrapper's timeout while the machine's disk was nearly full), median latency 71 s; the model answered 9 of 9 sequence tasks right by itself. 0 forbidden strings in requests or replies.

Caveats: one author wrote the worlds, the being, the methods and this measurement; the methods were tuned in two passes on two World v2 conditions (World O uses that tuning), some choices are still at the grid edge; "best method" is picked after the fact on the report seeds (favours the methods); the methods have no rule learning while playing, the being has; the MCTS reference has 200 iterations and is below the oracle-planner in World v2. The full table for every method and condition is in `docs/vs_world.md`.

Not measured: see `docs/vs_world.md`, section "Not measured" (deep RL beyond one small layer, a LinUCB planner with B7 rule use, MCTS in World O and the first world, World O with methods tuned on it, the LLM beyond 3 worlds and budget 60, rule learners outside the DSL, real data).

## Track B13: a context-aware chooser (synthetic worlds, author-defined)

Question: Track V1 found that where rules matter little the being's choosing part loses to a tuned LinUCB (World v2 current -0.18 to -0.38, the recommended profile only ties; first world at budget 600 -0.45; World L -0.07 to -0.21). Why, and can an opt-in change to the being's own chooser beat or tie LinUCB there while keeping the World O and rule-learning wins? Everything is the author's simulation (worlds, families, rewards, the being, the methods); no real data. Code: `kore-self/src/being/linval.rs` (new: the estimate, its tag, its controller key), switch-guarded branches in `world2/learner.rs`, `world2/engine.rs` (genesis tag), `world_o/engine.rs` (genesis tag), `planner.rs` (first world), `lookahead/beingl.rs` (World L), small read-only accessors in `world2/model.rs`, `model.rs`, `lookahead/beingl.rs`, the B13 key in `controller.rs`, the opt-in `chooser` argument of `being_run_v2` (`being_v2_tools.rs`); tests `being/tests_b13.rs`, `being/tests_b13_golden.rs`, one tool test in `being_v2_tools_tests.rs`; diagnosis and tuning `kore-self/examples/diag_b13.rs`; the V1 harness `examples/measure_vs_world.rs` with the B13 rows and the review modes `b13-v2`, `b13-o` added; the review baseline `being/vs_world/fallback.rs` (rules-or-LinUCB) and a read-only `LinUcb::score` in `vs_world/core.rs`. Branch `chooser-b13` from e9ed7d1d, 2026-11-07, Windows, 8 CPUs shared with other work. Tuning and diagnosis on seeds 101..120 only; report seeds 1..20, the V1 budgets and the V1 tuned methods (not re-tuned); 95% t-intervals, paired differences on identical worlds (better/worse/tie of 20).

```
cargo run -p kore-self --example diag_b13 --offline --release -- ablate-v2 | v2 | b2 | l | b2-disc       (diagnosis, tuning seeds)
cargo run -p kore-self --example diag_b13 --offline --release -- tune-v2 | tune-v2-ext | tune-b2 | tune-l | tune-l-ext
cargo run -p kore-self --example measure_vs_world --offline --release -- v2 | l | b2 | rules | o 600000 | b13-v2 | b13-o 600000   (report seeds)
cargo run -p kore-self --example diag_b13 --offline --release -- o        (World O check, tuning seeds 101..110)
```

### Step 1: diagnosis (tuning seeds 101..120)

`diag_b13 ablate-v2` scores every decision of a policy in World v2 with the TRUE expected value of every option on the same menu (the World v2 oracle's truth table, measurement only; the policy never sees it) and splits the loss against the best option on that menu by where it arises: attempts on cells (family, difficulty, strategy) with fewer than 3 earlier attempts ("young"), attempts on settled cells where the chosen offer was the best one but the strategy was not ("strategy"), and settled cells on another offer ("offer"). Loss is per unit of attempted energy (reward per energy given up at the same energy).

| World v2 (tuning seeds) | policy | true reward per energy | menu-choice loss | young cells | strategy on the best offer | another offer | skipped menus whose best option beat the life's rate, per 100 steps |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| small clean | ours current (B1 planner) | 2.785 | 0.302 | 0.168 | 0.041 | 0.093 | 4.72 |
| small clean | LinUCB (V1 tuning) | 2.797 | 0.168 | 0.142 | 0.001 | 0.025 | 1.33 |
| medium clean | ours current | 2.969 | 0.309 | 0.180 | 0.094 | 0.035 | 1.57 |
| medium clean | LinUCB | 3.047 | 0.133 | 0.113 | 0.002 | 0.018 | 1.14 |
| medium hard | ours current | 2.965 | 0.426 | 0.181 | 0.131 | 0.114 | 2.55 |
| medium hard | LinUCB | 3.068 | 0.274 | 0.148 | 0.022 | 0.103 | 5.03 |
| large clean | ours current | 2.925 | 0.440 | 0.169 | 0.227 | 0.044 | 4.17 |
| large clean | LinUCB | 3.180 | 0.096 | 0.082 | 0.001 | 0.012 | 0.51 |

* **The main loss is choosing the wrong strategy on the right offer in cells the being has already tried** (0.04 to 0.23 reward per energy against 0.001 to 0.022 for LinUCB), the second is exploring young cells (0.17 to 0.18 against 0.08 to 0.15). Lowering the B1 optimism makes it worse, not better (beta 0.5: the strategy loss rises to 0.29 to 0.51, reward -0.22 to -0.38): the B1 estimates of the strategies are only corrected through optimism, because each one rests on the few attempts of its own (family, difficulty, strategy) cell.
* **LinUCB's advantage is sharing across a family's difficulties, not its difficulty or type structure.** LinUCB variants on the same tuning seeds: family features only 2.908 / 3.068 / 3.145 / 3.153 (small clean / medium clean / medium hard / large clean), the V1 features 2.797 / 3.047 / 3.068 / 3.180, one parameter per (family, difficulty) cell like the B1 leaves 2.737 / 2.973 / 2.962 / 3.053 (about the being's level), type and difficulty structure without the family 2.71 to 2.80.
* **First world** (B2 families): there difficulty does matter (family features only: 2.78 at 600 and 2.91 at 3000, far below), and LinUCB with one parameter per (domain, difficulty) cell is the best variant (3.805 at 600, +0.50 over the B1 planner with the same cells): so the B1 estimator itself (each cell shrunk with a fixed weight 4 toward its domain's average, optimism 1.5 sd) explores and corrects worse than a ridge estimate with its width, even on the same cells. Removing the `discovered` arm gives +0.11 at 600 and -0.14 at 3000; the B11 skip fix +0.00 / +0.06.
* **World L**: the B1 cells are keyed by (family, strategy, previous family and result), 2F + 1 contexts per (family, strategy); LinUCB, which ignores the context, is 0.09 to 0.32 above the B1 planner. Not skipping helps the B1 planner in `keys` (+0.09).

So the cause is the same in the three worlds: the B1 model keys every estimate on one fine cell and shares only by a fixed-weight shrink toward that family's own average, so strategy comparisons rest on few attempts and many cells must be explored. LinUCB shares evidence across cells through a regression and measures its uncertainty from that regression.

### What was built (opt-in; off by default)

`linval.rs`, used by all three choosers (World v2 / World O, the first world, World L):

* Per strategy, a ridge regression (penalty 1 per feature, as LinUCB) of the being's REPORTED successes on visible features of the offer: bias, family, difficulty (World L: bias and family) and, optionally, the family type and type x difficulty. The cell itself is one more feature with penalty `cell_k`; by the block-inverse identity its estimate is `(cell_k x linear part + successes) / (cell_k + attempts)` (the B1 shrink, with the linear estimate in place of the family's average) and its width is `sqrt((cell_k / (cell_k + n))^2 x z'S^-1 z + 1 / (cell_k + n))` (exactly LinUCB's `sqrt(x'A^-1 x)` for that model; a test checks both against an explicit ridge regression fed one outcome at a time). `cell_k = 0`: no cell feature (pure linear).
* The chooser scores every option with `listed reward x clamp(p + alpha x width, 0, 1) / estimated energy` (the B1 score with LinUCB's optimism), keeps the B1 energy estimate and skip test (or the B11 settled test where the profile has it), and keeps the B7 rule-record estimate for `discovered` wherever a rule covers the offer. "Combined with our rule estimates" therefore means: rules where they apply, the shared linear estimate everywhere else.
* The fit is a pure function of the cell counts the being folds from its own log, so every decision is re-derived from the log alone (tested in World v2 and World O). Every decision revision states the estimate (`chooser_estimate`) and, for every alternative, `estimate_from_linear`: the linear part, each active feature with its weight and the attempts behind it, the cell's own attempts and successes, `cell_k`, the width, alpha and the optimistic p (or `estimate_from_rule` with the rule id and record).
* Switches: World v2 and World O genesis tag `w2_lin:a<alpha milli>/k<cell_k milli>/t<0|1>` (read back by the fold; with the switch off no tag and no word of the genesis text changes); first world `ModelChooser::lin` and World L `GreedyL::lin` (with `GreedyL::skip_rule`) are chooser constants, like the B11 skip fix there (the first world's and World L's genesis do not record the chooser, so they are not available through `being_run`). Controller key `context_chooser = on|off` (default off; a bad value makes the whole file unparseable; missing or unparseable file: off; asking for it when not allowed is a refusal, audited). The tool `being_run_v2` takes `chooser: "context"`; it is granted only with that key and only when the being is created (a later request for an existing being without it is refused as `fixed_at_creation`). KILL is checked before every step as before (tested with the switch on).
* With the switch off every chooser is byte-identical to e9ed7d1d: golden digests of a World v2 logged run, a World O logged run, a first-world logged run, World L logged runs in the four settings and measured lives of all four choosers were computed on e9ed7d1d and are pinned in `tests_b13.rs`.

### Tuning (seeds 101..120 only; objectives fixed before the runs)

Grid alpha 0.25 / 0.5 / 1, cell_k 0 / 1 / 4 / 16, types on / off, then a second pass beyond the edges of the first choice (as in V1). World v2 objective: mean over small clean, medium clean, medium hard, large clean, on top of the current learner and on top of the recommended profile. Chosen: alpha 0.5, cell_k 16, no type features (`LIN_V2`): current +0.182 [+0.059, +0.304] (15 of 20), recommended +0.167 [+0.051, +0.282] (17 of 20); the second pass (cell_k 64 and 256, alpha 0.35 and 0.7) changed the objective by at most 0.001 on top of the recommended profile and was lower on top of the current learner, so the first choice was kept. Type features were worse at alpha 0.5 and 1 in every pair (for example alpha 0.5, cell_k 16: +0.096 with them, +0.182 without) and slightly better at alpha 0.25, where every setting scored lower. First world (budgets 600 and 3000): alpha 0.5, cell_k 4 (`LIN_MENU`): +0.216 [+0.093, +0.339] (17 of 20), +0.212 with the skip fix. World L (four settings, budget 400): alpha 1, pure linear (`LIN_L`), +0.154 [+0.044, +0.264] over B1 with the B1 skip test and +0.170 [+0.061, +0.279] without skipping (17 of 20; the second pass, alpha 1.5 to 3, gave at most +0.001); not skipping was tuned like V1 tuned the methods' skip.

Same check on the decision-level probe (tuning seeds): with B13 the strategy loss on settled cells falls to 0.001 to 0.026 (from 0.04 to 0.23), the young-cell loss to 0.06 to 0.14, the total menu-choice loss to 0.07 to 0.24 (LinUCB 0.10 to 0.27; recommended + B13 0.07 to 0.21).

* **Negative result: the B13 chooser does not keep the World O win.** It costs -0.500 [-0.650, -0.351] against the current learner (worse in 19 of 20 worlds); with it the being is level with the best standard method (Thompson +0.040, MLP +0.097, intervals containing 0) and only just above LinUCB (+0.117) and linear Thompson (+0.101), and below the simple fallback (-0.081 [-0.155, -0.006]). The current learner stays the best of everything here (+0.42 over the fallback, +0.54 over Thompson).
* Cause (report-seed description, plus the tuning-seed check below): with the shared estimate a new family starts from what other families taught, not from an optimistic fresh cell, so the being tries far fewer families: 518 learnable families attempted over the 20 lives against 1,137 for the current learner (LinUCB 566); fewer families tried means fewer revealed examples and fewer rules, and in World O the rules are where the reward is (V1). Checked on tuning seeds 101..110 (300,000 energy, `diag_b13 o`): rules accepted per life 36 -> 18, attempts per sequence family 434 -> 314 and per compose family 238 -> 123 (slightly more on formula, grid and knapsack families), families reaching competence 239 -> 156 of about 516, reward per energy after the first 100k 4.036 -> 3.936. So the optimism of the B1 fresh cells, which costs reward in World v2, is what feeds the rule search in World O. B13 stays off by default, and its genesis tag records it where it is used; it should not be switched on for World O (not tried: B13 with an exploration bonus for new families, or with the B12 family-wide rules).

Rule learning on revealed examples does not involve the chooser; the `rules` report on this branch reproduces V1 exactly (B2 search 0.784 / 0.809 right with 4 / 32 clean examples, 0 wrong; B7 robust guard 0.773 / 0.809 under noise).

### Verdict

* **Cause found**: the B1 estimate rests on one fine cell per option and shares only through a fixed-weight shrink toward the same family's average; the being loses mostly by keeping a worse strategy on offers it already knows, and by exploring many young cells. LinUCB's edge was sharing across the cells of a family through a regression, with a width that measures what the regression knows.
* **The B13 chooser fixes it where rules matter little**: World v2 B13 profile above tuned LinUCB in 12 of 12 conditions (+0.12 to +0.29) and above the best method in 11 of 12; the chooser change alone ties LinUCB. World L: ties the best method in 7 of 8, slightly below LinUCB in one. First world: ties at 3000, **still loses at 600** (-0.30 against LinUCB, a negative result).
* **The World O win is not kept with B13 on**: current + B13 is -0.500 [-0.650, -0.351] below the current learner (19 of 20 worlds) and only level with the best standard method (Thompson +0.040); B13 makes the being try fewer new families, so it finds half as many rules. **The simple rules-or-LinUCB fallback ties or beats the B13 design in half the World v2 conditions** (B13 profile above it by +0.016 to +0.085, significant in 6 of 12) **and beats current + B13 in World O** (+0.081). B13 is therefore a World v2 / World L improvement of the chooser, opt-in, not a general one; rule learning is untouched.
* The choice stays explainable: every decision lists, per option, the linear part and every feature weight with the attempts behind it, the cell's own counts, the width and the optimism, or the rule and its record.

### Caveats

One author wrote the worlds, the being, the methods and this measurement. The B13 constants differ per world (World v2 / World O: alpha 0.5, cell_k 16; first world: alpha 0.5, cell_k 4; World L: alpha 1, pure linear, no skip), each tuned on that world's tuning seeds, as V1 tuned the methods per world; the methods were not re-tuned. The estimate uses the cell counts the being already keeps, so it inherits their properties: reported (noisy) outcomes, no forgetting under drift (World v2 drift conditions) except through B3b where that is on. Type features were tried and not used. In World O the switch was not tuned (World v2 constants), as V1 did for the methods. "Best method" is picked after the fact on the report seeds, which favours the methods.

### What is tested (not measured)

`being/tests_b13.rs`: with the switch off every chooser is byte-identical to e9ed7d1d (golden digests of World v2, World O, first-world and World L logged runs and of measured lives of all four choosers, computed on e9ed7d1d with `tests_b13_golden.rs`); the estimate equals an explicit ridge regression with a penalised cell feature fed one outcome at a time (mean, width and optimistic p, cell_k 0, 1, 4, 16); the tag round-trips and bad tags are refused; the World v2 genesis carries the switch (no tag when off); with the switch on (with the B7 profile) a World v2 run is deterministic, the unlogged measurement takes the same steps, the state folds back from the log with the switch, all 500 decisions are re-derived from the log, every decision revision names the estimate and gives for every alternative its features, weights, attempts behind them, cell counts and width (or the rule record); the kill switch stops before the next step and the stop is logged; World O with the switch folds, reads the switch from its genesis and re-derives all 1,500 decisions; the first-world and World L choosers with the switch are deterministic and explain their estimate; the controller key is validated (bad value: invalid file), off by default, fails closed when the file is missing or invalid, and a request without it is a refusal; `linval.rs` names no hidden world parameter. `being_v2_tools_tests.rs`: through the tool, `chooser: "context"` without the key runs with the B1 estimate and audits the refusal, a bad value refuses the run (fail closed), with the key the being is created with the switch and every decision replays, a later plain run keeps it, and a being created without it cannot get it later (audited). `tests_b13.rs` also checks that the rules-or-LinUCB baseline is deterministic and uses both rule answers and LinUCB choices.

### What B13 does not show

Anything outside these author-defined worlds; B13 combined with the B8 lookahead, B9 experiments, B3b adaptation or the B12 family-wide rules (with B12's chooser switches on, B12 decides); World O with B13 constants tuned on World O; the first world's genesis or World L's genesis recording the switch (they are chooser constants there, not available through `being_run`); budgets other than the V1 ones; real data.

## Track W1: World T, a sandbox world of data work (synthetic data, author-defined)

Question: in a more realistic sandbox of data work (tables with export quirks, time series, logs; nine task kinds with
exact checkers), does the being learn from its own log which tool or plan works for which kind of task, how does
it compare with standard methods on the same tasks, seeds and budgets, how robust is that to the reward design, and
are later task kinds learned faster? Design: `docs/world_t.md`. Code: `kore-self/src/being/world_t/` (new),
`src/world_t_sandbox.rs`, `src/world_t_tools.rs`, harness `kore-self/examples/measure_world_t.rs`:

```
cargo run -p kore-self --example measure_world_t --offline --release -- sweep  --home <scratch dir>
cargo run -p kore-self --example measure_world_t --offline --release -- report --home <scratch dir> --beta 2 --ucb-c 0.003 --lin-alpha 1
cargo run -p kore-self --example measure_world_t --offline --release -- ood    --home <scratch dir> --beta 2 --ucb-c 0.003 --lin-alpha 1
```

Measured 2026-11-08 (first pass 2026-11-07), branch `world-t` from 8591da53, Windows, 8 CPUs shared with other
builds, 4 threads. Budget 6000 energy per life; all kinds open by 60% of the life. Every file of a world was written
to a sandbox under a temp data root through `safe_path` and read back by every policy (each file read from disk
once per world and then kept in memory); removed after its world. Wall time: sweep 1053 s tuning + 340 s report;
main report 39 s; OOD 126 s. 95% t-intervals; paired differences on identical worlds (better/worse/tie of 20).

### Tuning separation and budget

Seeds 101..120 were used for tuning only; seeds 1..20 for reporting only (never for tuning). Budget 6000 in both.

Crossover points. Against LinUCB and UCB1 the ranking flips between penalty 1 and 3.16 x the listed reward (at energy
weights 0.316 and 1; at 0.1 the being still leads at 3.16), and at penalty 10 the being is behind both at almost
every weight. Against always SQL it flips only at penalty 10: at weight 0.1 (always SQL ahead by 1.31), 3.16 and 10
(ahead by 0.18 to 0.19), with ties at 0.316 and 1. **Region where an accuracy-first policy beats the being: penalty
10 x reward** (always SQL, which never answers wrong, earns more there at three of the five weights), and LinUCB and
UCB1 beat it from penalty 3.16 up. Why: with a harsh penalty the being over-skips (51% to 92% of tasks at penalty 10,
against 16% to 32% for the bandits). Its wrong-answer estimate starts from a pooled or flat prior of about 0.25 with
weight 2, so a plan it has not tried enough carries a large expected penalty and loses to the skip bar; the bandits
learn the penalty only from realized rewards and keep answering. Where the penalty is at most 1 x the reward the
being leads everywhere.

### Verdict

* At the default reward design (no penalty) and wherever the wrong-answer penalty is at most 1 x the listed reward,
  the being leads tuned LinUCB, UCB1 and always SQL at every energy weight from 0.1 to 10 (main point +0.127 over
  LinUCB), and is 0.69 below the reward-best oracle. Its lead there is plan choice and its own rules (series rules on
  72% of exact-series tasks, precision 1.000 before the checker), not skipping.
* **Negative: with a harsh penalty (3.16 x the reward at weights 0.316 and 1, and 10 x at almost every weight) the
  being loses to LinUCB and UCB1, and at 10 x always SQL beats it at three of five weights.** It over-skips: its prior
  for the wrong-answer chance makes untried plans look too risky. The being leads on 22 of 30 grid points against
  LinUCB, 24 against UCB1, 25 against always SQL.
  (Track W1b: the cause was the optimism bonus on the right-answer chance only; fixed there, 25 / 30 / 29 of 30.)
* Accuracy is traded for reward unless wrong answers cost something: 11.2 wrong answers per 100 tasks at no penalty,
  0.1 at penalty 10 (where the being is the most accurate policy and earns the least).
* Later kinds are not learned faster (negative); the pooled prior does not raise reward at the main point (-0.023
  [-0.067, +0.020]), helps out of distribution (+0.074 [+0.012, +0.136]).
* Out of distribution the being stays ahead (+0.52 over LinUCB), mostly by skipping; the verified searches stay at
  precision 1.000.

Caveats: one author wrote the data generator, the quirks, the tools, the learner, the references and this measurement;
plan outcomes are deterministic given the file (no checker noise); the sniffing loader was written for these quirks;
equal but small tuning budgets (6 configurations), UCB1 at its grid edge at 15 of 30 points; the reward-best oracle uses
its own running rate, a strong reference but not a proven optimum; the SQL timeout is enforced after the query
returns; one life length (6000).

Not measured: real data of any kind; a language model as a planner or as an SQL writer; noise in the checkers; menus of
several tasks; drift of the quirks over the life; longer lives; the logged run at full length through the gate (tests
run it for 40 + 10 steps; the measurement runs are in memory with the same steps, a test checks it); a prior for the
wrong-answer chance tuned to the penalty (the likely fix for the harsh-penalty region); the timeout under real engine
slowness.

## Track W1b: World T over-skipping at harsh penalties (value-scale optimism)

Pre-registered 2026-11-08, before any run on the report seeds 1..20 with the fix (only tuning seeds 101..120 had been
run). Success, judged only against this: (1) the being is no longer significantly behind tuned LinUCB or UCB1 at any
sweep point with penalty >= 3.16 x reward (upper end of the paired 95% interval >= 0); AND (2) the headline (penalty 0,
energy weight 1; at abd8de1e +0.127 [+0.084, +0.171] over LinUCB) is not significantly worse (paired interval of new
minus old being includes 0 or is above 0); AND (3) the number of the 30 sweep points where the being is ahead of
LinUCB (interval above 0) does not drop below 22.

Root cause (`kore-self/src/being/world_t/learner.rs`, `estimate`, at abd8de1e lines 145-147): the score was
`(min(1, p + beta x sd) x reward - p_wrong x penalty) / energy`. The optimism bonus sat on the right-answer chance
only, at the reward's scale; the penalty term was a point estimate from a prior of 0.25 (weight 2). With a penalty of
10 x reward an untried plan scored about `(0.5 + bonus) x R - 2.5 R < 0`, below the skip bar, so the being skipped;
a skipped task yields no outcome, so the wrong-answer estimate never moved (and series tasks skipped yield no
examples for the rule search). The bandits put their bonus on the realized reward (UCB1 rescales it by the penalty
range; LinUCB's wrong-answer mean starts at 0). Fix (`value_ucb`, default on, World T only): the bonus is on the
expected reward of the whole outcome (right +R, wrong -P, no answer 0; Dirichlet posterior with the same counts and
prior), `min(R, p R - p_wrong P + beta x sd) / energy` with `sd^2 = (p(1-p) R^2 + q(1-q) P^2 + 2 p q R P) / (w + n + 1)`.
With no penalty this is exactly the old score (test
`value_ucb_is_identical_without_a_penalty_explores_the_penalty_term_and_old_logs_keep_their_rule`; sweep: 0/0/20 ties
at all five penalty-0 points). No controller key: no other world and no live World T run changes (the tool's runs
have penalty 0); logs without the `wt_ucb` tag replay with the old rule.

Measured 2026-11-08 at commit a5f834bf (code; branch `wt-overskip` from abd8de1e), Windows, 6 threads. Same protocol
as Track W1: every policy re-tuned at every point on seeds 101..120 (6 configurations each; the old being tuned
separately with its own 6 betas), reported on seeds 1..20, budget 6000, paired 95% t-intervals, (wins/losses/ties of
20). The old being re-run here reproduces Track W1 exactly (22 / 24 / 25 points ahead of LinUCB / UCB1 / always
SQL). Before this run on the report seeds, the fix had been run only on tuning seeds 101..120 (penalties 3.16 and 10,
betas 0.5 to 8). Tuning wall 2629 s, report 766 s.

success criterion is not met; the over-skipping is largely removed (skip share at penalty 10, weights 0.1 to 3.16:
51-81% -> 14-18%) and 5 of the 7 losses to LinUCB are gone, 2 small ones remain.

## Track B14: a persistent rule library and always-on curiosity (synthetic first world, author-defined families and rewards)

Question: in long runs of the first world (the long run's being: extended2 families, chooser `model`, discovery every 10 steps, composition and pruning under the long-run controller, budget 3000 with refills) reward per energy stops improving early. Can (1) a rule library in the being's own log (indexed by context, reused in new contexts after a check, retired on evidence) and (2) a small curiosity budget that never runs out make it keep improving? Everything is the author's simulation; no real data. Code: `kore-self/src/being/b14/` (new: `library.rs`, `curiosity.rs`, `ctl.rs`, `measure.rs`, `tests.rs`), small switch-guarded hooks in `being/loop.rs` (Engine field `lib`, `run_full` setup and passes, extra decision citations from the rationale key `b14_cites`, curiosity energy), additive fields and fold rules in `being/state.rs`, key validation in `being/controller.rs`, the opt-in `rule_library` / `curiosity` arguments of `being_run` (`being_tools.rs`), harness `kore-self/examples/measure_b14.rs` (modes `diag`, `arms`, `transfer`, `short`). Branch `b14-rules` from abd8de1e, 2026-11-08, Windows, 8 CPUs shared with two other agents. Tuning on seeds 101..120 only; report seeds 1..20; 95% t-intervals; paired differences on identical worlds, (wins/ties/losses of n). Rule worlds = worlds where an oracle that holds the oracle book earns at least 0.1 more reward per energy than the same oracle without rules (a property of the world, fixed before the runs); the other worlds are simple worlds.

```
cargo run -p kore-self --example measure_b14 --offline --release -- diag --seeds 101..120 --steps 100000 --window 10000
cargo run -p kore-self --example measure_b14 --offline --release -- arms --seeds 101..120 --steps 60000 --post 20000 --arms base,lib+cur20:0,lib+cur20:1,lib+cur20:3,lib+cur5:1,lib+cur50:1
cargo run -p kore-self --example measure_b14 --offline --release -- arms --seeds 1..20 --steps 200000 --window 10000 --post 50000 --arms base,lib,cur20,lib+cur20
cargo run -p kore-self --example measure_b14 --offline --release -- transfer --seeds 1..20 --steps 30000 --every 1000 --source-steps 50000
cargo run -p kore-self --example measure_b14 --offline --release -- short --seeds 1..20
```

### Pre-registered success criteria

Pre-registered 2026-11-08 before report-seed runs (given by the reviewer, copied verbatim; judged only against them):

> PRIMARY: paired difference (B14 on minus B14 off, same seeds/worlds) in mean true reward per energy over the post-plateau part of the run (steps 50k..end of the long run), report seeds 1..20: 95% CI lower bound > 0 AND at least 14 of 20 wins. If not met, B14 "did not beat the plateau" — say so.
> SECONDARY: (a) slope of windowed reward over 50k..end with B14 on: 95% CI above 0 (vs baseline slope, also reported); (b) curiosity cost on already-solved worlds: paired loss no worse than 1% of baseline reward per energy (CI upper bound of the loss < 1%); (c) transfer: steps-to-competence on a new family with library vs without, paired CI; (d) no significant regression on vs-world / World O / World v2 (CI includes or is above 0).
> Report every claim in the same format: mean [95% CI] (wins/ties/losses out of 20), seeds, budget/steps, commit.

Operational choices (the criteria text was saved before any report-seed run; the choices below for (b) and (c) were fixed while the first report-seed run was still running, before any of its output was read): "B14 on" = library and curiosity (`lib+cur20`), "off" = the long-run being as it is (`base`); the long run is 200,000 steps (windows of 10,000; the slope is the least-squares slope of the window means from 50k on, per 100k steps); "already-solved worlds" = the simple worlds (rules can add less than 0.1 there), and the cost of curiosity there is `lib+cur20` against `lib` (library on in both, so only curiosity differs), relative to `lib`; "new family" = each of the 14 expressible hidden families in a new world, competence = the rule book answers at least 90% of 40 fresh tasks of the family right (checked every 1,000 steps, not reached = 30,000); the source of the library is a 50,000-step B14 life in world seed + 500.

### Step 1: the plateau, reproduced (tuning seeds 101..120, base being, 100,000 steps)

`measure_b14 diag` (the long run's being in-process, windows of 10,000 steps; reference: a renewal oracle that knows the hidden success rates and holds an "oracle book", the being's own search run by the author on 60 sampled tasks of every hidden family):

| steps | reward per energy | regret vs oracle with book | live rules | families covered (of 14) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0k-10k | 3.947 [3.481, 4.414] | 0.580 [0.385, 0.775] | 2.9 | 2.6 |
| 40k-50k | 3.927 [3.456, 4.399] | 0.599 [0.401, 0.798] | 3.0 | 2.8 |
| 50k-60k | 3.935 [3.467, 4.404] | 0.592 [0.395, 0.788] | 3.0 | 2.8 |
| 90k-100k | 3.939 [3.465, 4.413] | 0.588 [0.393, 0.782] | 3.0 | 2.8 |

The curve is flat from the first window on (in this setting the plateau starts before 10,000 steps, not at 50,000). Cause (per-world tables of the mode): sequence difficulties 2 to 5 get 10 to 30 revealed examples early (the fixed strategies fail on most of their families), are then skipped for good, so their signatures (four families each) never reach the B2 support and get no rule; and where a rule exists the `discovered` strategy is almost never chosen (its cell restarts from a pooled prior when a rule is accepted; world 116: four rules at difficulty 2, one `discovered` attempt there in 30,000 steps). Families covered at the end: 2.8 of 14.

### What was built (each a switch, off by default)

| part | what it does |
|---|---|
| library estimate | where a live rule applies to the offered prefix, the `discovered` strategy is estimated from the rule's own record on the revealed examples times the record of all rule-produced answers (planner optimism and skip test unchanged); the decision cites the rule's note and the latest examples of its record |
| library retirement | a live rule whose latest 6 applicable revealed examples (at least 4) have a 95% Wilson upper bound of share right below 0.5 is retired (`rule_retired`, tag `by:library`, revision citing every example of the window) |
| library reuse | imported entries (`rule_lib_import` notes) and rules of the same difficulty of the other sequence domain are candidates; one becomes a rule after 1 training + 1 held-out exact reproduction on the being's own examples, never applicable-and-wrong (B2 guard and spare equations); `rule` note tagged `via_library`, revision citing the import note and the examples |
| curiosity | energy at most `pm` per mille of the energy spent so far (the budget never runs out); value = expected information gain about the offer's rule (B9 live hypotheses) + `ei_w` x expected improvement / rate; fires when value >= 0.05; policy `b14-curious`; the decision records the value, its parts, the planner's choice and the budget |
| controller | `rule_library`, `curiosity`, `max_curiosity_energy_pm` (hard max 100); fail closed; the setup is fixed at creation (`b14_setup` note); a controller that later no longer allows it gives a logged refusal and the run goes without it |

Tuning (seeds 101..120, 60,000 steps, post part from 20,000; minus base): `lib+cur20` with `ei_w` 0 / 1 / 3: +0.482 / +0.492 / +0.479; `pm` 5 / 20 / 50 (ei_w 1): +0.479 / +0.492 / +0.490; `lib` alone +0.300, `cur20` alone +0.365. ### Against the pre-registered criteria

* PRIMARY: +0.491 [+0.287, +0.695] (18/0/2 of 20), seeds 1..20, 200,000 steps, commit a062a62a: **met** (lower bound > 0, 18 >= 14 wins).
* (a) slope over 50k-200k with B14 on: -0.013 [-0.030, +0.003] per 100k steps (baseline -0.005 [-0.016, +0.005]; difference -0.008 [-0.026, +0.009], 7/0/13): **not met**. B14 raises the level within the first 10,000 to 20,000 steps; improvement does not continue past 50k, the curve is flat at the higher level.
* (b) curiosity cost on already-solved (simple) worlds, lib+cur20 relative to lib, n = 6, seeds 1, 2, 5, 11, 12, 16, 200,000 steps: +2.5% [-1.9%, +6.8%] (4/0/2; worst world -0.35%): the loss's upper bound is 1.9%, above 1%: **not met** (no loss on the mean, but with 6 worlds the interval cannot rule out a 1% loss).
* (c) transfer: steps to competence saved with the library vs without, +475 [-128, +1,078] (7/10/3 of 20), 30,000 steps: interval contains 0; **no established speed-up** from importing a library.
* (d) vs-world, World O, World v2: the B14 code is not reachable from the World v2, World O, World T or V1 method engines, and with B14 off the first world is the planner bit for bit (test `off_is_the_planner_bit_for_bit`; the golden-digest tests of earlier tracks pass unchanged, 595 of 595 kore-self tests): the difference is exactly 0 by construction (not re-run, so no interval). Not regressed; B14 was not tried in those worlds.

### Verdict

B14 lifts the plateau's level but not its slope: +0.49 reward per energy over steps 50k-200k (18 of 20 worlds, all 14 rule worlds), regret against the oracle with the book 0.576 -> 0.085, families covered 4.3 -> 11.6 of 14; the gain arrives early and the curve is then flat again (slope criterion not met). Both parts help alone (library +0.29, curiosity +0.35) and more together. Curiosity spends about 0.1% of the energy. Importing a library into a new world gives no established speed-up, because curiosity already finds the rules within about 1,000 steps. The cost criterion on solved worlds is not met at n = 6 (point estimate a gain). Short budgets: no loss (+0.04 at 600, +0.15 at 3000).

### Caveats

Author-defined world, families, grammar and rewards; the oracle book (60 tasks per family, searched jointly per difficulty under the never-wrong guard) is weaker than the being's own book in some worlds, so the regret is a reference, not a bound; the 0.1 threshold gives only 6 simple worlds; the long run is in-process (no 200,000-step logged run; tests run the logged path for up to 2,500 steps, with cold restarts); B5 pruning merges rules on logged examples and can lower coverage; curiosity constants tuned at 60,000 steps; one source world per target for transfer.

### What is tested (not measured)

`being/b14/tests.rs` (12 tests, temp dirs only): every earlier opt-in key and the B14 keys parse together; each key given twice, bad values and values above the hard maximum make the file invalid and fail closed; off is the planner bit for bit over 1,500 steps; the curiosity budget holds and does not run out; library candidates need the being's own examples and are blocked by one applicable-and-wrong example; imports are logged once, checked, reused with citations of the import note and the examples, and fold back; library uses cite the rule note; retirement on evidence cites every example and folds back; a logged run equals 400 + 500 steps with a cold restart; not allowed = refused, logged and off (missing, invalid and silent controller; allowed at creation and switched off later); B14 needs the extended world; KILL stops after 40 steps; old logs fold with no B14 state; import tags round trip and a tampered id is refused; the B14 sources read no hidden world parameter and use no file, network or process API.

## Track E1: evolutionary search over the rule DSL (synthetic first world, author-defined families, expression language and rewards)

Question: B14 lifts the first world's long-run plateau but the slope after 50k steps stays flat; the remaining sequence families are not covered by rules, and some (the negative controls) are outside the B2 grammar and composition. Can evolutionary search (genetic programming) over the being's rule DSL (populations of candidate rule expressions, mutation, crossover with each other and with the being's verified rules as inherited genes, selection by exact matches on the being's own training examples) find NEW rule forms that the enumerative discovery cannot, under the existing verification path, inside a bounded compute budget, and does that raise reward and keep it improving?

### Pre-registered success criteria

Pre-registered 2026-11-08 before report-seed runs (given by the reviewer, copied verbatim; judged only against them):

> PRIMARY = paired difference (B14+E1 on minus B14 on, same worlds) in mean true reward per energy over steps 50k..200k, report seeds 1..20: 95% CI lower bound > 0 AND >=14/20 wins. SECONDARY: (a) slope of windowed reward 50k..200k with E1 above B14's slope (paired CI); (b) families covered by verified rules increases (paired CI); (c) 0 wrong rules accepted (precision before checker reported with N, rejected count); (d) evolution compute cost reported (time and energy share) and no significant loss on simple worlds; (e) no regression in World T / vs-world / World O / World v2 (by construction or measured). Tune only on seeds 101..120. Every claim: mean [95% CI] (wins/ties/losses of 20), seeds, steps, commit. A negative result is acceptable and must be reported honestly.

### Results (report seeds 1..20)

Setup: commit d04e1441 (tuned defaults from seeds 101..120: pass every 100 steps, population 48, 24 generations, target signature weighted by unexplained examples, budget 20 per mille), `measure_e1 arms --seeds s..s --steps 200000 --arms b14,b14+e1` run once per seed (windows of 10,000 steps, post part from step 50,000, coverage on 40 fresh tasks per family). Arms: B14 on (library + curiosity 20 per mille) and the same plus E1, same worlds. 14 rule worlds (oracle book gain >= 0.1: seeds 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, 13, 14, 15, 17, 18, 19, 20), 6 simple worlds (1, 2, 5, 11, 12, 16). Nothing was tuned on seeds 1..20. Paired differences: mean [95% CI] (wins/ties/losses of 20), E1 minus B14.

| criterion | result | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| PRIMARY: reward per energy, steps 50k..200k | B14 4.272 [3.947, 4.597], B14+E1 4.329 [3.991, 4.667]; difference **+0.057 [+0.010, +0.104] (14/1/5 of 20)**; relative +1.29% [+0.20%, +2.38%]; rule worlds +0.083 [+0.019, +0.147] (12/0/2 of 14), simple worlds -0.004 [-0.011, +0.004] (2/1/3 of 6) | **met** (lower bound > 0, and 14 of 20 wins, exactly the threshold) |
| (a) slope of windowed reward 50k..200k (per 100k steps) | B14 -0.013 [-0.030, +0.003], B14+E1 -0.024 [-0.053, +0.006]; difference -0.010 [-0.039, +0.018] (10/1/9 of 20). One world (19) falls hard with E1 (slope -0.259 against +0.005) | **not met** (the slope stays flat; E1 does not make it keep improving) |
| (b) families covered by verified rules at the end (>= 0.9 of fresh tasks right) | the 14 grammar families: 11.55 -> 12.20, difference +0.65 [+0.38, +0.93] (12/8/0); all 18 (with the 4 negative controls outside the B2 grammar): 11.55 -> 13.75, difference +2.20 [+1.62, +2.78] (18/2/0). Families an evolved rule answers >= 90% of (count of worlds): PatFib, NegProd, NegLcg, NegMod7, Ext2CubeGeom, Ext2ParityCubic, ExtPeriodic | **met** |
| (c) wrong rules accepted | 65 evolved rules accepted over 20 worlds, **0 wrong** on 200 fresh tasks per family (65 checked); 27,549 candidates sent to the B2 check, 753 rejected by it; precision before the checker on the being's later revealed examples 244,382 / 244,382 = 1.000; answers given through evolved rules 178,291, judged right 172,926 (0.970, includes execution slips of the world) | **met** |
| (d) compute cost and simple worlds | energy-equivalent share (evaluations at the author-set 1,000 per energy unit, over energy spent) 0.018 [0.015, 0.021]; evolution wall time 339 s [227, 450] of a 925 s [623, 1,227] life (time share 0.35 [0.29, 0.41]; B14 alone 445 s); 23,971 passes in total. Simple worlds: relative -0.09% [-0.29%, +0.10%] (2/1/3 of 6) | **met** as pre-registered (cost reported, no significant loss on simple worlds); the cost is large in wall time (about 2x the B14 run) |
| (e) no regression in World T / vs-world / World O / World v2 | by construction, not measured: E1 is off by default behind fail-closed controller keys (`evolution`, `evolution_budget_pm`); with it off the run is step-for-step the B14 run (test `off_is_run_b14_step_for_step`); `Form::Gp` is never produced with E1 off, and the V1 brute-force baseline returns None for it | **met by construction** (not re-measured in those worlds) |

Caveat on the primary (not pre-registered, reported because it changes the reading): the reward per energy above counts only the energy of world steps; the evolution compute is a budget in energy-equivalents and is **not** charged to the being. If it is charged at the author-set rate (the life share of each world, 0.02 in 19 of 20 worlds), the difference becomes -0.021 [-0.065, +0.024] (5/1/14 of 20): the measured gain (+1.3%) is smaller than the compute it costs (1.8%). The exchange rate is an author choice, so this is a sensitivity check, not a verdict.

Reading: evolutionary search finds rules the enumerative discovery cannot (mostly PatFib and three of the four negative controls), safely (0 wrong of 65, precision 1.000 before the checker), and lifts the level of the plateau slightly in rule worlds; it does not make reward keep improving after 50k steps (slope criterion not met), costs about a third of the wall time, and its reward gain does not exceed its own compute at the author-set exchange rate. Wall time of the report run: 7,404 s (20 single-seed processes, 4 at a time, one thread each).

## Not measured

Real-life data of any kind (the free-text section above is also synthetic); the probabilities of the live ledger (`predict_make`/`predict_score` have not been run on real data; the S4 numbers above are synthetic sequences only; the older `self_ledger_snapshot` rows are not scored by any measurement); behaviour with
the being loop in any world other than the author-defined simulation (no real tasks, no language-model thinker or advisor: the B4 advisor is simulated, a real model's quality as an advisor is unmeasured); very large logs; sensitivity to the synthetic generator's choices (150 days, Poisson counts).
